blk_part_02_part_2_fruit_inside_rich_mea.text: Fesenjan is a sweet-and-sour Iranian stew from Gilan. It is a khoresh, an Iranian stew served over rice. Its main mix is pomegranate juice or paste, ground walnuts, and poultry such as duck or chicken. It can also contain other meats. Unlike melon with ham, the fruit becomes part of the sauce and gives flavor to the whole dish.

In Thailand it is called som tam, the Thai name for this sour, salty, and spicy salad. The mix includes sour lime, hot chili, salty fish sauce, and a little palm sugar. Dried shrimp may also be included.

blk_part_03_part_3_fruit_with_fish_salt_.text: Chamoy offers another surprising use of fruit. Chamoy is a Mexican sauce made from pickled fruit, salt, and chili. Fruit is packed in brine, which is salty water used for pickling, sometimes with vinegar. The fruit brine is then seasoned with chili powder. The finished sauce can be put on fresh fruit, adding salty, sour, sweet, and spicy flavors.

Sam Panopoulos is credited with making the first one at the Satellite Restaurant in Ontario in 1962. He tried the mix because Canadian Chinese dishes often combine sweet and sour flavors. The name came from the canned pineapple brand he used, not from the state of Hawaii.
